chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding

a man who bought a slave girl and she bore him a child, then it was found that she had been stolen. He (peace be upon him) said: The master takes the slave girl, and the man takes his child by paying her price.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a man buys a slave girl who turns out to be stolen and has already borne him a child?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'ghasb' (unjust possession) in commercial transactions, distinguishing between the restitution of the primary asset and the retention of the offspring as a separate entity. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential approach to balancing the rights of the original owner against the purchaser's good faith, ensuring that the child is not treated merely as an accessory to the stolen property. This precedent is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for determining compensation values in cases of defective sales involving livestock or slaves.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding

a man who buys a slave girl and she gives birth for him, then he finds out she had been stolen’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The slave girl would be taken by her master, and the man would take his child with his price’.
en.sarwar: Aban has narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “About the case of a man who buys a pregnant slave-girl and does sexual intercourse with her when he did not know, abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He must return her and clothe her.’”
